articles.fullText:
(ECNS)-- On November 6, 2026, Belgium and Chile issued a joint statement merging their respective bids to host the BBNJ Secretariat. Under this new arrangement, Belgium cedes the Secretariat seat to Chile, while asserting that the "physical and technical infrastructure for the Clearing House Mechanism" will be installed in and operating from Brussels. The two countries also offer to host meetings of the Subsidiary Bodies in Brussels, subject to relevant decisions by the Conference of the Parties (COP). The proposal is framed as "a contribution to facilitating an effective decision at COP 1."
The geopolitical calculation behind this move is obvious and understandable.
Belgium has struggled to craft a narrative that resonates with developing States. Its difficult fiscal and social situation in recent weeks has further dimmed its prospects in the bidding contest. Chile, while backed by some developing countries in Latin America and elsewhere, lacks ready-built infrastructure dedicated to accommodate the Secretariat. Multiple public debates at the United Nations have noted that both Brussels and Valparaíso are losing their first-mover advantage vis‑à‑vis Xiamen, China's candidate city. Prior to the November 6 statement, several analytical models ranked Xiamen as the frontrunner.
With two months remaining before the convening of COP 1 -- at which the BBNJ Agreement mandates a decision on the Secretariat seat -- Belgium and Chile have aligned their campaigns to combine their respective strengths with an aim to alter the trajectory of the race.
This tactical arrangement is undeniably shrewd.
Belgium shakes off the full burden of hosting the Secretariat and instead seeks custody of the Clearing House Mechanism, widely seen as the centrepiece of the BBNJ Agreement. The statement does not state explicitly that Belgium is withdrawing its bid; it merely transfers the privilege of hosting the Secretariat to Chile. This approach allows the two States to preserve, to the maximum extent possible, the support they have already secured, particularly among EU Member States.
Chile, meanwhile, can leverage infrastructure based in Brussels to mitigate the practical challenges of the Secretariat's early operational phase, given its lack of dedicated premises. Notably, the statement highlights the "operationalization of the financial mechanism" as a core function of the Chile‑hosted Secretariat, with no comparable emphasis on other Secretariat functions. This indirectly confirms that the country's focus is on the substantial financial prospects under the BBNJ Agreement.
That said, the new joint proposal raises significant legal and practical concerns.
· The BBNJ Agreement unambiguously confers upon the COP, not any individual Party, the authority to determine the modalities of the Clearing House Mechanism in a decision separate from that on the Secretariat seat. Belgium and Chile conflated the two distinct issues and struck a backroom deal on the installation and operation of the CHM in Brussels, amounting to a pre-emptive determination that encroaches on the decision‑making prerogative of the COP, which comprises not only Belgium and Chile, but also more than 100 other Parties to the Agreement.
· A central priority for developing States is the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from activities with respect to marine genetic resources (MGRs) and their digital sequence information (DSI) of areas beyond national jurisdiction, notably access to marine data and information. Given the European Union's well-known conservative stance and stringent regulatory framework governing cross-border data and information flows, Parties -- in particular developing States -- have reasonable grounds to question whether they will enjoy unimpeded access to MGRs and DSI stored in and managed from Belgium.
· As emphasized during the most recent session of the BBNJ Preparatory Commission (PrepCom) held in March, the prevailing view is that the Secretariat must be able to function immediately, for which infrastructure readiness is indispensable. While the joint proposal addresses hosting arrangements for Subsidiary Body meetings, it remains silent on the absence of dedicated office accommodation for the Secretariat itself.
· Should COP 1 adopt this joint proposal, the nascent Secretariat would need to conclude two separate headquarters agreements: one with Chile and one with Belgium. It is far from certain that the two States would accept identical terms, given their distinct legal systems and institutional practices. Furthermore, Secretariat officials and technical staff based in Valparaíso would have to travel frequently to Brussels, on the other side of the globe, to oversee the CHM. Amid pervasive fiscal constraints, this raises legitimate questions about whether the Secretariat can operate cost‑effectively from its inception.
In sum, Belgium and Chile's initiative carries a positive dimension: Belgium's de facto step back from the contest to host the seat of the BBNJ Secretariat improves the prospect of reaching consensus on the matter. At the same time, the joint candidature gives rise to meaningful concerns regarding its legality and operational viability. The United Nations Division for Ocean Affairs and the Law of the Sea (DOALOS), acting as the interim BBNJ Secretariat, could furnish a legal opinion on the validity of the proposal ahead of any COP decision. Should the Parties choose to proceed with this proposal, they must give thorough consideration to the substantial complications and high costs that would follow.
The author, Yu Minna, is an associate professor at the Law School of Ocean University of China. The views do not necessarily reflect those of ECNS.

articles.title: Chinese envoys step up peace efforts in Middle East, Horn of Africa

articles.summary: Chinese envoys step up peace efforts in Middle East, Horn of Africa
articles.summaryCn: 随着中东和海湾地区冲突进入第八个月，中国加强外交努力，特使访问多国，呼吁对话与和平，并提出区域和平稳定方案。

paragraphs.en: As conflicts in the Middle East and Gulf region enter their eighth month, their {{0}} effects continue to spread, with rising {{1}} in Yemen and the Red Sea adding to challenges facing the Horn of Africa. Against this backdrop, China has stepped up {{2}} efforts to ease regional tensions. Zhai Jun, special {{3}} of the Chinese government on the Middle East issue, Liu Xianfa, special representative of the Chinese government on African affairs, and Hu Changchun, special envoy for the Horn of Africa Affairs of the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, recently visited seven countries across the Middle East, the Gulf, the Red Sea and the Horn of Africa, {{4}} with regional parties and calling for dialogue and peace. In an exclusive interview with China Media Group (CMG) after their visits, the three envoys {{5}} China's diplomatic efforts, the challenges to achieving a lasting ceasefire and the country's proposals for regional peace and {{13}}. Supporting regional countries in resolving disputes through dialogue
Since September, clashes involving Yemen's Houthi group, Saudi Arabia and Yemeni government forces have {{6}}, while security risks in the Red Sea have also increased. Conflicts across the Middle East remain {{7}}, raising concerns over further regional spillover. During his recent visits to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia, Chinese envoy Zhai met with officials from the three countries and discussed the situation in Yemen with relevant parties, explaining China's positions and proposals. Zhai said China believes that the use of force cannot resolve disputes and that escalating regional instability serves no one's interests. He called on all parties to exercise {{8}}, avoid further tensions and seek solutions through diplomatic channels.

支持地区国家通过对话解决争端
自9月以来，涉及也门胡塞武装、沙特阿拉伯和也门政府军的冲突加剧，红海安全风险也随之上升。中东各地的冲突仍然相互关联，引发对地区进一步溢出效应的担忧。在最近访问伊朗、阿曼和沙特阿拉伯期间，中国特使翟隽会见了三国官员，与有关各方讨论了也门局势，阐释了中国的立场和建议。翟隽表示，中国认为使用武力无法解决争端，地区不稳定升级不符合任何人的利益。他呼吁各方保持克制，避免进一步紧张，通过外交渠道寻求解决方案。

paragraphs.en: Zhai said China's diplomatic engagements had reinforced the sense that peace, development and the ability to determine their own future are shared aspirations among people in the Middle East. He outlined China's approach to mediating regional issues, including supporting Middle Eastern countries in pursuing strategic {{9}}, unity and self-reliance, while opposing external {{10}}. China also encourages regional countries to resolve disputes through dialogue and {{11}} based on the merits of each issue, he said. Against this backdrop, China has stepped up diplomatic efforts to ease regional tensions. Zhai Jun, special envoy of the Chinese government on the Middle East issue, Liu Xianfa, special representative of the Chinese government on African affairs, and Hu Changchun, special envoy for the Horn of Africa Affairs of the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, recently visited seven countries across the Middle East, the Gulf, the Red Sea and the Horn of Africa, engaging with regional parties and calling for dialogue and peace.
In an exclusive interview with China Media Group (CMG) after their visits, the three envoys outlined China's diplomatic efforts, the challenges to achieving a lasting ceasefire and the country's proposals for regional peace and stability.

Supporting regional countries in resolving disputes through dialogue
Since September, clashes involving Yemen's Houthi group, Saudi Arabia and Yemeni government forces have intensified, while security risks in the Red Sea have also increased. Conflicts across the Middle East remain interconnected, raising concerns over further regional spillover.
During his recent visits to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia, Chinese envoy Zhai met with officials from the three countries and discussed the situation in Yemen with relevant parties, explaining China's positions and proposals.
Zhai said China believes that the use of force cannot resolve disputes and that escalating regional instability serves no one's interests. He called on all parties to exercise restraint, avoid further tensions and seek solutions through diplomatic channels.
Zhai said China's diplomatic engagements had reinforced the sense that peace, development and the ability to determine their own future are shared aspirations among people in the Middle East.
He outlined China's approach to mediating regional issues, including supporting Middle Eastern countries in pursuing strategic autonomy, unity and self-reliance, while opposing external interference. China also encourages regional countries to resolve disputes through dialogue and consultation based on the merits of each issue, he said.
China has put forward a series of proposals since April, including a four-point proposal on promoting peace and stability in the Middle East, the four principles for resolving the Palestinian question, and a four-point proposal on a new security architecture for the Middle East.
Zhai stressed that lasting stability requires common security among regional countries. He called on the international community to address the Palestinian question, which he described as a root cause of instability in the Middle East, and take into account the links between regional conflicts.

Horn of Africa must not become a geopolitical battleground

With disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz amid the prolonged conflict, the Red Sea has become increasingly important. Rising tensions there pose serious risks to trade, investment, energy and food security in the Horn of Africa.
Liu said China had proposed the Outlook on Peace and Development in the Horn of Africa to support regional countries in addressing security, development and governance challenges independently and collectively.

Hu said security challenges remain the biggest obstacle to development and revitalization in the Horn of Africa and across the continent. He stressed the importance of strategic autonomy, Pan-Africanism and greater unity among African countries.
China's strong political trust and practical cooperation with its 53 African diplomatic partners provide a solid foundation for its constructive participation in addressing regional issues, Hu said.
China also supports regional development by helping countries address development gaps and reduce the conditions that fuel conflict. Chinese peacekeepers in missions in Darfur, Sudan and South Sudan have also contributed to maintaining peace and stability, he added.
Liu acknowledged that significant challenges remain to achieving lasting peace in the Horn of Africa. China is ready to work with all countries and people committed to peace and development to implement the Global Security Initiative and contribute to Africa's prosperity and long-term stability, Liu said.

The 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change concluded in Antalya, Türkiye, without reaching consensus on political decisions. This marks the first time since 2009 that a UN Climate Change Conference has failed to strike a deal. Building consensus for climate governance has become an even more intricate and daunting challenge than climate action itself. A questionnaire survey conducted by CGTN among 10,032 respondents across 40 countries shows that the importance of energy issues in climate governance has risen significantly. Energy transition has become an urgent challenge for all countries to address, and the strategic status of new energy is particularly prominent.
The COP31 Closing Plenary Session is held in Antalya, Türkiye, November 22, 2026. 
The issue of fossil fuels has been the focus of negotiations at this conference. Countries including France and Panama issued a joint letter calling for the agreement to clearly set out a path toward transitioning away from fossil fuels. Saudi Arabia and other major oil-producing countries, however, argue that fossil fuels will continue to play a role in the economy for some time to come. According to the poll, 77.8% of respondents believe that the traditional fossil energy supply crisis has become a practical global challenge. When evaluating the "biggest challenges facing global energy development in the next decade," climate change and environmental impact ranked first, followed by affordability of energy prices and energy supply security in second and third places. The latter two account for nearly 40% of responses, while the top three together account for 77.7%.
Meanwhile, 77.3% of respondents agree that transforming the energy system toward a cleaner, more diversified and more efficient model is an important way to address global energy challenges. Another 74% expect the importance of new energy in the global energy system to continue to rise in the next decade, with 42.6% anticipating a significant increase. The proportion of respondents from Global South countries selecting "significant increase" exceeds 50%, while respondents from developed countries are relatively conservative: only 32.9% anticipate a "significant increase," and nearly 20% choose "basically unchanged." articles.fullText:
The Japanese government has come under fire for featuring a YouTuber known for promoting conspiracy theories and unverified claims in a public campaign promoting its national security policy. The move has sparked criticism of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's administration.
The YouTuber, Naokiman, is a Japanese content creator with more than 2.5 million subscribers to his main channel. His videos cover a range of topics, including conspiracy theories and claims whose credibility have been questioned. The government campaign featuring him, however, focuses on issues such as Japan's national security and energy security.
While the government says the initiative aims to reach younger audiences and raise public awareness of security issues, some members of the Japanese public have questioned the credibility of the campaign and whether public funds should be used for such publicity.
A Japanese resident told China Media Group (CMG) that public funds should be spent on education and social welfare rather than promoting increased defense spending. The resident also questioned the government's choice of a YouTuber whose credibility has been called into question to communicate serious national security issues.
Another Japanese resident told CMG that the government should take into account how its security policies and military expansion plans might be perceived by neighboring countries and the potential implications for regional relations.
A Chinese expert has also criticized the government's approach, saying it uses sensationalized, entertainment-oriented methods to package serious security issues and normalize military expansion.
Meng Mingming, a Japan affairs expert at the Institute of Japanese Studies of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, said the Takaichi administration was seeking to capitalize on the popularity of online influencers to promote its right-wing agenda through emotional appeals and fan-based engagement.
At the same time, the approach was intended to weaken domestic opposition by using entertainment-oriented messaging to lower public vigilance and resistance, Meng said. The ultimate goal, he argued, was to make Japanese society increasingly accustomed to military buildup and pave the way for revisions to the country's three key security documents by the end of the year.
Assessing the potential consequences, Meng said the use of social media influencers for public opinion mobilization had indeed attracted considerable attention and generated widespread discussion, potentially providing Japan's right-wing forces with a new means of advancing what he described as a process of "neo-militarism."
However, the strong public backlash also showed the limits of the government's strategy, he said.
"As military expansion and preparations for war increasingly affect the everyday interests of ordinary Japanese people, they will eventually see through these tactics," Meng said, adding that the campaign could ultimately trigger an even stronger public backlash against the Takaichi administration.

周一，中国外交部长王毅与瑞士联邦委员会副主席兼外交部长伊尼亚齐奥·卡西斯在江苏省南京市共同主持第五轮中瑞外长级战略对话。王毅同时也是中共中央政治局委员，他表示中瑞关系的发展体现了中国外交的若干原则。王毅说，这些原则包括：大小国家一律平等、反对强权政治；尊重各国自主选择发展道路、不干涉内政；以及发挥互补优势，实现互利共赢。王毅表示，尊重彼此核心利益是中瑞关系的政治基础。

他补充说，中方希望瑞方采取具体行动反对“台独”，支持中国的国家统一事业。王毅还表示，中瑞合作的成功经验再次表明，保护主义并非万能药，相互交织的利益不应被框定为安全风险。“开放合作是超越零和陷阱、迈向共赢未来的正确道路，”他说。上月，中国和瑞士签署了升级自由贸易协定的议定书。根据该议定书，双方将作出高标准承诺，进一步开放货物贸易、服务贸易和投资，同时升级涵盖原产地规则、贸易便利化、技术性贸易壁垒、数字贸易、竞争以及贸易与可持续发展等领域的规则。

瑞士是中国在欧洲的第七大贸易伙伴，而中国是瑞士在亚洲的最大贸易伙伴。2025年双边贸易额达到490.4亿美元。在周一的会晤中，王毅还表示希望瑞士在帮助中欧解决经贸分歧方面发挥积极作用。他敦促中欧超越“贸易失衡”的叙事陷阱，通过对话协商妥善处理分歧，扩大合作范围以实现互利共赢。王毅表示，中国愿加强与瑞士的战略沟通，践行真正的多边主义，改革和完善全球治理，维护国际公平正义，并补充说两国应共同努力，为动荡的世界带来更大的稳定性和确定性。
